title: Bounded admin connection review, not automatic cleanup
summary: Admin connection-hygiene inspects explicit IDs or an opt-in bounded tenant inventory, historical recency, complete owner-role projections and target metadata similarity. Missing/partial evidence stays unknown; cleanup/grant previews require review and approval, never execute or certify unused connections.
selection: Delegated reads require an authorized Fabric admin context AND Tenant.Read.All or Tenant.ReadWrite.All; a Fabric audience or directory-role claim alone does not prove usable admin API authorization. An authenticated context can still return AUTH_REQUIRED. Supported service-principal authorization is a separate route. Ask for an approved context instead of requesting consent, changing roles or switching identities automatically.

Use admin connection-hygiene --id <CONNECTION_ID> (repeatable) OR --inventory, not both. Inventory is an explicit tenant-admin opt-in, never an automatic fallback from regular connection diagnostics or permission failure. No workspace flag is accepted. Every explicit ID must be distinct, non-zero and fit connection-limit; no silent subset truncation of explicit IDs.

Defaults are 10 connections (maximum 20), 3 pages per inventory/role list (maximum 20), 20 roles per connection (maximum 100), and a TOTAL 30-second read deadline (maximum 300). Role reads grow only within these bounds. --all/--force do not override scope limits or apply actions. Aggregate hygiene cannot resume one continuation cursor; use admin list-connections for page resumption.

Read only admin connection/role metadata. Inventory mode reuses list rows rather than N extra shows. Pagination uses validated same-route opaque tokens, never response continuation URLs (even a URL pointing at regular connections). URI-only, malformed/cyclic/partial/error-bearing projections stay unknown. --dry-run is an offline validated read-scope preview.
interpretation: Use unused-days (default 90, 1-36500) only as a historical review threshold. created-after cannot precede the reliable 2026-05-01 boundary or lie in the future. Missing/malformed/future/conflicting events are unknown, not never-bound/never-used proof. Explicit null post-cutoff events mean no event was reported, not absence of ALL current dependencies. Recency may lag and legitimate seasonal connections may look old.

Only COMPLETE recognized role projections establish reported owner counts or single-individual continuity risk. Missing roles, unknown principal/role types, conflicting assignments, scope mismatches and partial pages stay unknown. Owner/PendingOwner are distinct; observed pending handoff suppresses retirement and new-owner previews. A principal assignment is not directory existence, employment, membership, credential health or source authorization.

Similar target metadata groups compare type/path/connectivity/gateway inside the selected scope, without emitting names, paths or secrets. This is not interchangeable credentials, privacy/security settings, grants, or complete dependency coverage. No keepId/winner/redundant connection is selected and no rebind is performed.

status summarizes only requested observations: ready is not end-to-end health. --strict prints the report and fails for review findings or unknown evidence; inspect partial and each check, not only the summary. Missing myRole is not treated as loss of admin authority, because admin access and regular effective role are different.
review_plan: reviewPlan is ALWAYS applied:false and readyToApply:false. Actions have requiresApproval:true and blockers. Historical retirement signals plus complete, non-pending ownership can yield a guarded admin delete preview, never eligibility to delete. Full dependency review, owner consent and human approval remain unverified blockers. Unknown ownership never produces deletion/ownership mutation previews.

Ownership-continuity previews leave a supported durable owner identity explicitly missing. Admin add-connection-role-assignment supports User/ServicePrincipal, NOT Group. The service-principal template is an example, not an automatically selected principal or auth-mode change. It is only offered for known shareable types; personal/unsupported types require review instead. Admin Owner requests may remain PendingOwner until credential handoff, so a grant response is not effective ownership or working credentials.

Concrete mutation previews and templates keep BOTH --readonly and --dry-run, requiresApproval, destructive metadata and read-only verifyAfter. The top/report-plan destructive flag describes proposed irreversible retirement previews, not mutation by the hygiene command itself. Neither dry-run previews nor available admin authority authorize removing the guards and applying changes.

No apply/delete/grant/transfer/rebind/credential test, principal lookup, credential write or source authorization probe runs. Use existing mutation commands only as separate explicitly reviewed operations.
legacy_helpers: connection find-stale/find-duplicates/find-single-owner are caller-visible legacy candidate helpers, not bounded admin coverage. find-stale now excludes malformed timestamps instead of turning parse failures into never-bound/never-used candidates. Their candidate/keep heuristics are review signals, not delete eligibility or credential equivalence. Use the admin review command when admin evidence and explicit partial/unknown reporting are required.
